subject: RE: demo - real workspace
text:
Hi Carl –

Sorry I didn’t respond yet as I’m still in the process of exploring various tools and capabilities for an upcoming video-based object tracking project (actually unrelated to our work at FYR Medical). Coincidentally I also happened to connect with Nick Rajpal via LinkedIn recently, and when I noticed he works at Encord I also mentioned the same to him.

I will say this: from my brief exploration, the Encord workflow looks awesome. However I’m specifically looking for (hopefully) a solid toolset for annotating lots of video footage, training YOLO models, and deploying to edge devices. I’m not sure Encord can handle the deployment side. I’m also hoping to identify either a free or very-low-cost solution as this project is currently a bootstrapped effort until I can get a prototype off the ground. So it’s unclear whether Encord is a good fit for my needs right now.

Anyway, thanks for checking in, and let me know if you have any ideas for this. Otherwise, I’ll definitely keep an eye on this as the project moves forward. Great job on the Encord system and best of luck to you and your team.

- Mark

Mark A. Lamkin
Co-Founder & CTO   |   FYR Medical
(817) 903-2571

subject: Re: Nice to meet on Friday
text:
Hey James,
Thank you for reaching out to schedule a follow-up call. Not going to do the call this week as I would like to have more info and clarity first. What would the purpose be of this, for a demo?

We currently anticipate requiring approximately 5,000–10,000 hours of audio files to be annotated over the next 12 months. This could evolve rapidly as we onboard indie artists. For growth projections, we expect a 20–30% increase in annotation volume over the year. Is this sufficient for you guys?

We can enrich the labels with existing metadata from the songs including things like BPM, key. This might prove helpful for annotators. We require more manual intervention for subjective info like energy (On a 1-10 scale) and keywords that will form the basis of training packs. For example a film score dataset might include songs that are instrumental but also listenable on their own independent of being synced.

Anything else I’m missing? I am new to data labelling in general so any guidance is appreciated.

Byron Polley ❖ www.polyphonic.io <https://polyphonic.io/> ❖ +27 83 286 5231

subject: Re: Encord/Mobbin - Website/App Annotation
text:
Hi Alex,

Apologies regarding the silence on our end and thanks so much for following up with us over the past few weeks.

After considering all options, we decided to keep our annotation tool in-house using a blend of low-code platforms like Retool and custom-building only the core areas (e.g. annotation UI), which will help us keep development costs whilst still keeping agile.

One of the key deciding factors was tool flexibility—we wanted to be able to bend our tools to our needs quickly rather than to be dependent on the release cycle of a 3rd party tool.

I really appreciate your team's eagerness to learn about Mobbin and our data annotation needs over the past few weeks!

Best,
Jian Jie Liau
